reading: The grid is split into bands of two colours; each band holds one or more single marker cells. From every marker draw all four diagonals to the grid border; each diagonal cell takes the marker colour assigned to the band it lies in (band colour -> colour of the marker found in that band), so a line changes colour when it crosses into the other band.

slots.source: the odd-coloured single cells (markers) inside the two-colour band layout
slots.lines: the four diagonal rays from each marker, running to the grid border
slots.colour: per-cell key: band colour -> colour of the marker that sits in that band (learned per pair, not constant)

why: every changed cell lies on a diagonal through some marker, and its new colour is the marker colour of the band it is in

reading: The 3x3 input is placed at the top-left of a doubled (6x6) background canvas and every coloured cell is extended diagonally down-right in its own colour until it reaches the canvas border.
why: each fg cell's down-right diagonal is its own colour up to the border of the 2H x 2W canvas; nothing else is coloured

reading: Keep only the middle column of the (odd-width) grid; every cell outside the centre column is cleared to background 0.

new_rows.name: offcol
new_rows.datalog:
w(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
mid(X) :- px(Y, X, C), w(W), S = X + X, S = W.
offcol(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !mid(X).

why: all cells outside the centre column become 0; centre-column cells are unchanged

reading: Each 0-coloured bracket (3x3 head holding 7/9 contents) has a one-cell-wide 0 tail running to the opposite grid border. The tail is erased and the head (with its contents, same orientation) is translated along the tail line to the far border where the tail ended.

slots.subject: each 3x3 bracket head of colour 0 with its enclosed cells, sitting on a grid border
slots.path: the straight 0 tail leaving the head and reaching the opposite border
slots.target: the far border at the tail's end; the head's outer edge lands on that border
slots.rest: tail and old head position cleared to background 7

why: each head keeps its shape and contents and ends flush with the opposite border; tails disappear; objects without tails are untouched
invariants: lone 9 cells / 99 pieces with no tail

reading: Rows (or columns) that have a 4 at both grid-border ends are lanes; inside a lane the colours are swapped 0<->8 and 6<->7. Everything else is unchanged.

new_rows.name: lane
new_rows.datalog:
w(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
h(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
four(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), C = 4.
hrow(Y) :- four(Y, X0), X0 = 0, w(W), four(Y, W).
vcol(X) :- four(Y0, X), Y0 = 0, h(H), four(H, X).
lane(Y, X) :- hrow(Y), px(Y, X, C), !four(Y, X).
lane(Y, X) :- vcol(X), px(Y, X, C), !four(Y, X).

why: every lane cell of colour a becomes key(a) with key {0:8, 8:0, 6:7, 7:6}; cells outside lanes never change

reading: Around every isolated 1 stamp a fixed plus: 2 above, 7 left, 6 right, 8 below (clipped at the grid edge).
why: each 1 is the centre of an identical cross 020/716/080; all other cells stay

reading: The empty interior of the 2-coloured rectangle is filled with 2, except the bounding box of the 5 cells, which keeps its 0s and 5s.

new_rows.name: hole
new_rows.datalog:
two(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), C = 2.
five(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), C = 5.
fy0(min(Y)) :- two(Y, X).
fy1(max(Y)) :- two(Y, X).
fx0(min(X)) :- two(Y, X).
fx1(max(X)) :- two(Y, X).
vy0(min(Y)) :- five(Y, X).
vy1(max(Y)) :- five(Y, X).
vx0(min(X)) :- five(Y, X).
vx1(max(X)) :- five(Y, X).
inbox(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), vy0(A), vy1(B), vx0(P), vx1(Q), Y >= A, Y <= B, X >= P, X <= Q.
hole(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), C = 0, fy0(A), fy1(B), fx0(P), fx1(Q), Y > A, Y < B, X > P, X < Q, !inbox(Y, X).

why: every 0 strictly inside the 2-frame and outside the 5s' bounding box becomes 2; nothing else changes
invariants: 5 cells and the 0s inside their bounding box

reading: The 5x5 input uses one colour; the output is a fixed 3x3 glyph of 5s chosen by that colour: 1 -> plus (050/555/050), 2 -> T (555/050/050), 3 -> corner (005/005/555).

slots.key: the single non-background colour of the input
slots.glyph: 3x3 pattern of 5 on 0 looked up from that colour (1 plus, 2 T, 3 bottom-right corner L)

why: the output depends only on the input's foreground colour; the cell layout of the input is irrelevant

reading: Count the 2-coloured T shapes by orientation: stem-up (020/222) and stem-down (222/020). The 3x6 output shows the stem-up count as 3s in the left 3x3 block and the stem-down count as 1s in the right block, placed at block corners in the order top-left, bottom-left (for 2), then top-left, top-right, bottom-left (for 3), all four corners (for 4).

slots.objects: T-tetromino shapes of colour 2 (counted by pattern match, since some touch diagonally)
slots.classes: stem up -> colour 3, left block; stem down -> colour 1, right block
slots.display: count n drawn as n marks on the corners of a 3x3 block: 1 TL; 2 TL,BL; 3 TL,TR,BL; 4 all corners

why: the number of 3s equals the number of stem-up Ts and the number of 1s the number of stem-down Ts on every pair

reading: Each multi-coloured template shape appears once complete; elsewhere a few of its cells (e.g. its 8s, 4, or diagonal 2s) appear alone. Each partial fragment is completed into a full copy of its template, aligned so the fragment cells coincide with the matching template cells.

slots.templates: every complete multi-coloured component (one or two per grid)
slots.fragments: small single-colour pieces matching a sub-pattern of a template
slots.placement: translate the template so its matching cells cover the fragment; paint the rest of the template, keep everything else

why: after completion every fragment is part of an exact copy of a template; templates themselves are unchanged (pair 2 also turns the template's corner 3 at (4,3) into background, which looks like a data quirk)
